turns.query: Compare FY2024 SBA 7(a) lending geography with the same insured bank's 2025-06-30 Summary of Deposits geography across the 50 states and District of Columbia. Preserve every reported SBA row, use the canonical unpadded FDIC certificate to match lenders, and use SOD's state-abbreviation-to-state-FIPS correspondence for the 51-jurisdiction QCEW bridge. Retain lenders present in both sources with at least 500 FY2024 SBA rows. Within each lender form approval-dollar and branch-deposit-dollar state distributions, calculate total-variation distance as one half of the sum of absolute share differences, and rank descending with lender name and FDIC certificate ascending as tie-breakers. Define distribution overlap as the jurisdiction-wise sum of the smaller approval and deposit shares, equivalently one minus TVD. Report the eligible-lender count; leader name and certificate; its SBA row count, gross approvals, deposits, positive-approval and positive-deposit jurisdiction counts, TVD, distribution overlap, and TVD margin over the runner-up. Explain what the computed distance says about where this lender books loans versus where it gathers money, and what it cannot be stretched to show.

claims.description: The response uses the computed TVD and overlap to characterize the selected lender's project-state approval and branch-location deposit share mass as nearly disjoint.

If the response claims that the two state distributions trace particular SBA loans to particular depositors, it qualifies that claim because the aggregate source tables contain no loan-to-depositor linkage.

If the response calls the geographic TVD a funding-liquidity mismatch measure, it qualifies that interpretation because branch-location deposits and project-state approvals do not measure the bank's full funding or liquidity position.

turns.query: For that selected lender, identify its largest-approval jurisdiction and report its approvals, approval share, deposits and deposit share. Separately identify its largest-deposit jurisdiction and report its deposits, deposit share, approvals and approval share. Break any state-level tie by USPS abbreviation ascending. Explain which side of the two distributions drives the turn-1 distance result.

claims.description: The response uses the selected state decomposition to show that the deposit distribution is geographically concentrated while the SBA approval distribution is broad, rather than attributing the high distance to a small rounding residual.

turns.query: Overlay the preliminary retrospective 2025 QCEW private-employment vintage. For every one of the 51 jurisdictions, calculate 2024-to-2025 growth from annual-average employment levels and define the negative-growth set from the unrounded level calculation. Report the matched-jurisdiction count and negative-growth count. For the selected lender, report within that set the SBA row count, gross approvals, share of all its FY2024 approvals, gross approvals minus SBA-guaranteed approvals, SOD deposits and share of all its deposits. Also report the negative-growth jurisdiction with its largest approval dollars and that jurisdiction's calculated employment growth, breaking an approval tie by USPS abbreviation. Explain the grain and vintage limits of this macro overlay.

claims.description: The response treats annual state private-employment growth as a jurisdiction-level retrospective screen and not as the economic path of each loan, borrower, branch or approval during its origination year.

turns.query: Match the selected FDIC certificate to the 2024-12-31 Call Report and report the match count, RSSD ID, legal name and domestic-office total equity. Then run a sensitivity: assume a loss equal to 10% of the prior turn's gross-minus-guaranteed FY2024 approvals in negative-employment jurisdictions, hold everything else fixed, and report the loss, pro forma domestic-office equity, and loss as a percentage of reported equity. Explain what this calculation does and does not establish about the bank's credit loss and capital position.

claims.description: The response characterizes the final calculation as a static assumption applied to approval flow against reported domestic-office equity and recognizes that approval flow is not retained exposure or realized loss.

If the response attributes losses or borrower performance to the state employment screen, it qualifies that inference because the aggregate retrospective association does not establish a loan-level causal effect.

judge_reference.source: Frozen SBA 7(a), 2025 SOD, preliminary retrospective QCEW and 2024-12-31 Call Report tables
facts: Nineteen lenders qualify. Northeast Bank (FDIC 19690) has 2,552 SBA rows, 0.289033 billion USD approvals, 3.405883 billion USD deposits and 99.7440% TVD, 0.5975 point above the runner-up.
California has the largest approval amount and Maine has all reported branch deposits. Maine represents 100% of deposits but only 0.2560% of approvals.

Thirteen jurisdictions have negative calculated private-employment growth. They contain 738 Northeast SBA rows, 0.088294 billion USD approvals, 30.5479% of its approvals, 0.017450 billion USD unguaranteed approvals, and no reported SOD deposits.

The Call Report match is RSSD 468806, NORTHEAST BANK, with 0.444101 billion USD domestic-office equity. The 10% sensitivity loss is 0.001745 billion, reducing pro forma equity to 0.442356 billion, or 0.3929%.
known_overclaims: Treating branch deposit geography as the actual funding source for specific SBA loans.
Treating state employment growth as a borrower-level condition or causal driver.
Treating FY2024 approvals as year-end retained credit exposure.
Calling the mechanical loss an observed loss or regulatory-capital calculation.
